question.problem:
Let $a$ be a positive integer. Construct an expression that gives a two-digit number consisting of the last two digits of $215a.$

$$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}{{field-3}}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let $b=215a.$ Note that $b$ is positive. Now, let ${d}_{4},$ ${d}_{3},$ ${d}_{2},$ and ${d}_{1}$ be the last four digits of the number $a:$ 

$$
a=…{d}_{4}{d}_{3}{d}_{2}{d}_{1}
$$

Then, $a$ can be written in expanded form as

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⋯+1000{d}_{4}+100{d}_{3}+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} \\  & =100(⋯+10{d}_{4}+{d}_{3})+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the residue of $a$ modulo $100:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & ≡100(⋯+10{d}_{4}+{d}_{3})+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100) \\  & ≡0\cdot (⋯+10{d}_{4}+{d}_{3})+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100) \\  & ≡0+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100) \\  & ≡10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1}$ is the two-digit number consisting of the last two digits of $a.$

Finally, since $b=215a,$ and 

$$
215≡15\,(\text{mod}\,100)
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100) \\ 215a & ≡10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100) \\ 15a & ≡10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,100)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the expression that gives the last digit of $215a$ is the following:

$$
15a\,\text{mod}\,100
$$

Let $b=16a-13.$ Note that $b$ is positive. Now, let ${d}_{3},$ ${d}_{2},$ and ${d}_{1}$ be the last three digits of the number $b:$ 

$$
b=…{d}_{3}{d}_{2}{d}_{1}
$$

Then, $b$ can be written in expanded form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =⋯+100{d}_{3}+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} \\  & =10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the residue of $b$ modulo $10:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0\cdot (⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${d}_{1}$ is the last digit of $b.$

Finally, since $b=16a-13,$ and 

$$
16≡6,\,-13≡-3\,(\text{mod}\,10)
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 16a-13 & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 6a-3 & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the expression that gives the last digit of $16a-13$ is the following:

$$
6a-3\,\text{mod}\,10
$$

question.problem:
Let $a$ be a positive integer. Construct an expression that gives the last digit of $15a.$

$$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}{{field-3}}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let $b=15a.$ Note that $b$ is positive. Now, let ${d}_{3},$ ${d}_{2},$ and ${d}_{1}$ be the last three digits of the number $b:$ 

$$
b=…{d}_{3}{d}_{2}{d}_{1}
$$

Then, $b$ can be written in expanded form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =⋯+100{d}_{3}+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} \\  & =10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the residue of $b$ modulo $10:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0\cdot (⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${d}_{1}$ is the last digit of $b.$

Finally, since $b=15a,$ and 

$$
15≡5\,(\text{mod}\,10)
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 15a & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 5a & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the expression that gives the last digit of $15a$ is the following:

$$
5a\,\text{mod}\,10
$$

question.problem:
Let $a$ be a postive integer. Construct an expression that gives the last digit of $12a+11.$

$$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}{{field-3}}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let $b=12a+11.$ Note that $b$ is positive. Now, let ${d}_{3},$ ${d}_{2},$ and ${d}_{1}$ be the last three digits of the number $b:$ 

$$
b=…{d}_{3}{d}_{2}{d}_{1}
$$

Then, $b$ can be written in expanded form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =⋯+100{d}_{3}+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} \\  & =10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the residue of $b$ modulo $10:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0\cdot (⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${d}_{1}$ is the last digit of $b.$

Finally, since $b=12a+11,$ and 

$$
12≡2,\,11≡1\,(\text{mod}\,10)
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 12a+11 & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 2a+1 & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the expression that gives the last digit of $12a+11$ is the following:

$$
2a+1\,\text{mod}\,10
$$
